title: From Gravitational Action to Physical Scattering
overview: When does an interaction derived from a gravitational action support physically meaningful incoming and outgoing scattering states?
question: What additional boundary, constraint and asymptotic structures turn a source-derived kinematic scattering calculation into a physical scattering system?
foundation: The developing CH program has constructed source-derived one-particle and Bose-pair carriers and progressively stronger kinematic wave and scattering results; its existing physical-action and boundary investigations identify further constraints.
limits: Kinematic wave or scattering operators are not by themselves a constraint-preserving physical gravitational S-matrix. The direct matching of a full nonlinear action-derived boundary phase to the existing W6 carrier encounters a source-specific obstruction; physical phase-space, Bose-pair, flux and BRST conditions remain to be established.
next: Construct an action-derived physical phase space and boundary flux law, establish constrained Bose-pair and BRST-compatible interaction transport, and investigate the existence of physical and celestial scattering observables.

claims.statement: Continuing formally checked research develops source-derived kinematic asymptotic structures.
claims.scope: Specified W6/CH24 source carriers and kinematic scattering results; no physical S-matrix or published CH Paper IX claimed.

claims.statement: A source-specific boundary-carrier mismatch motivates an enlarged physical scattering construction.
claims.scope: Formal obstruction in a particular original-action representation, not a universal impossibility of gravitational scattering.

obligations.question: Develop an original-action boundary phase space with coupled Euler/flux constraints.
Establish physically constrained incoming/outgoing wave operators and compatible Bose-pair/BRST descent.

obstructions.summary: A direct full nonlinear boundary-frame identification fails on a specified source phase chart, necessitating a more suitable physical carrier.

relationships.summary: Both programs investigate continuation and boundary structure; a common physical mathematical bridge remains to be proved.

history.summary: CH scattering registered as a distinct research stream associated with, but not identical to, the site's celestial research program.
